predecessors.name: Timurid Empire
predecessors.text: Babur's Kabul, Kandahar and the Punjab, held before Panipat

predecessors.name: Lodi dynasty
predecessors.text: the sultanate of Delhi round Delhi and Agra after Ibrahim Lodi's defeat at Panipat

successors.name: British Raj
successors.text: Delhi city and its territory, the last Mughal land, taken over after the Rebellion of 1857

successors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
successors.text: Delhi after the Siege of Delhi (21 September 1857), taken by the East India Company

ledger.x: 1526: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat and founds the Mughal Empire.
21 April 1526: the Lodi sultanate of Delhi falls to Babur at Panipat.
1526-1527: Babur takes Gwalior and Bayana (entered under 1527, 'before Khanwa').
January 1528: Babur takes Chanderi and eastern Malwa.
1529: Babur's realm reaches the frontiers of Bengal and Bihar.
ledger.cp: Afghan and Rajput holdings east and south of Agra

ledger.x: Dec 1530: Humayun succeeds Babur (26 December) and the infobox moves the capital from Agra to Delhi ('Agra: 1526-1530; Delhi: 1530-1540'); the Humayun page still calls Agra 'the Mughal capital' and has him crowned at Agra Fort, so the seat is uncertain.
1535: Humayun takes Mandu and Champaner from the Sultan of Gujarat.
1536: Bahadur Shah retakes Gujarat.
June 1539: Sher Shah and Humayun meet at Chausa.
17 May 1540: Humayun is 'soundly defeated' by Sher Shah at Kannauj; the Mughal Interregnum begins.
17 May 1540: Hindustan passes to the Sur and Humayun goes into exile.
July 1540: the Mughals abandon the Punjab.
October 1545: Humayun takes Kandahar from the Persians.
18 November 1545: Humayun enters Kabul.
Nov 1545: Kabul becomes Humayun's seat for the rest of the Interregnum (he returned there in December 1553 and set out from it for the 1555 reconquest).
22 June 1555: Humayun wins at Sirhind.
23 July 1555: Humayun sits again on the throne in Delhi.
23 July 1555: the Interregnum ends.
July 1555: the seat returns to Delhi; Humayun dies at Sher Mandal, Delhi, on 27 January 1556.
5 November 1556: Akbar's regent Bairam Khan wins the Second Battle of Panipat.
1557: Kandahar passes to the Persians.
1557: the Mughals take Ajmer and Nagaur.
1560: the capital is Agra again; Akbar's Fatehpur Sikri follows from 1571.
1560: Akbar sends his armies against Baz Bahadur of Malwa.
1561: Malwa is annexed.
1561: Malwa becomes a Mughal province.

1562: the Mughal invasion of Marwar begins (infobox 'Mughal invasion of Marwar (1562-1583)'); the page gives no sieges or lands, only the span and that from 1561 the Mughals 'actively engaged the Rajputs in warfare and diplomacy' and most Rajput states accepted Akbar's suzerainty.
1564: the Gond kingdom of Garha falls.
1563-64: the Mughals occupy Jodhpur.
1567: the siege of Chittorgarh begins; the page gives 'a siege of four months' ending in February 1568, so the start (October 1567) is counted back, not stated.
1568: Ranthambore.
February 1568: Chittorgarh falls.
February 1568: Akbar takes Chittorgarh from Mewar.
1571: the court moves to Fatehpur Sikri; the Akbar page has Akbar lay 'the foundations of a new walled capital' in 1569, 'soon abandoned'.
14 February 1571: Bhadrajun falls.
1572: Akbar marches on Gujarat.
2 September 1573: 'The outnumbered Mughal army won a decisive victory on 2 September 1573.'
September 1573: Gujarat becomes a Mughal province; the Gujarat dossier closes the sultanate in 1573.
1574: war for Bihar and Bengal.
1574: Patna and Bihar are taken from Daud Khan Karrani.
1575: after Tukaroi the Karrani keep only Orissa.
1576: Rajmahal ends the war (infobox 'Rajmahal (1576)'; 'The Mughal army was subsequently victorious at the Battle of Tukaroi in 1575').
1576: Bengal is conquered from the Karrani sultan; Cliopatria shows it only from 1579.
September 1576: the Mughals hold Gogunda, Udaipur and Kumbhalgarh.
August 1581: Akbar seizes Kabul.
1583: the Mughal invasion of Marwar ends.
1583: Akbar recognises Udai Singh.
1585: the war for Kashmir.
1585: Pratap recovers much of Mewar.
1586: the capital is Lahore; the Akbar page has the capital 'moved to Lahore in 1585' and Akbar there for thirteen years.
June 1589: 'In June 1589, Akbar travelled from Lahore to Srinagar to receive the surrender of Yaqub.'
June 1589: Kashmir surrenders.
1591: Sindh submits.
1595: Baluchistan.
1595: Akbar's siege of Ahmadnagar.
1595: Chand Bibi cedes Berar.
1595: Orissa ceases to be a fief.
1595: Orissa passes from the Karrani remnant to direct Mughal rule.
18 April 1595: Kandahar returns to the Mughals.
1598: the capital is Agra again; the Akbar page says 'In 1599, Akbar moved his capital back to Agra, where he ruled until his death.'
8 April 1599: Akbar occupies Burhanpur.
August 1600: 'A subsequent revolt forced Akbar to take the fort in August 1600.'
August 1600: Ahmadnagar fort falls to Akbar.
17 January 1601: Asirgarh falls and Khandesh is annexed.
17 January 1601: Asirgarh falls and the occupation becomes annexation.
1615: Amar Singh submits and Chittor is returned.
November 1615: the Mughals attack the Ahom frontier.
June 1622: the Safavids take Kandahar.
1632: Daulatabad.
1635: Golconda submits.
1636: Bijapur submits ('...and then Bijapur in 1636').
October 1636: Shahaji surrenders Mahuli and Junnar.
October 1636: the Nizam Shahi remnant is partitioned.
1638: Ali Mardan Khan hands Kandahar to Shah Jahan.
1639: the court is at Delhi, Shahjahanabad; the Shah Jahan page is silent on the move.
February 1639: the Treaty of Asurar Ali.
February 1639: western Assam passes to the Mughals.
1646: Shah Jahan invades Bukhara's Balkh and Badakhshan.
1647: the Mughals withdraw.
22 February 1649: the Safavids take Kandahar.
22 February 1649: Kandahar is lost to the Safavids; Aurangzeb's campaigns of 1649 and 1652 fail.
29 September 1653: 'Mughals finally gave up all attempts to recover Kandahar' after Dara Shikoh's five-month siege.
1657: Aurangzeb takes Bidar.
1658: the Ahoms expel the Mughals from Guwahati.

c. 1656-1659: the northern frontier of Golconda. Siege of Golconda page: Aurangzeb 'besieged Golconda in 1656; the siege was withdrawn and a peace treaty established by Shah Jahan'; the page gives no terms and no territorial cession; the Aurangzeb…
1662: Mir Jumla takes Guwahati.
1662: the Mughals hold Garhgaon.
January 1663: the Treaty of Ghilajharighat.
1666: Shaista Khan takes Chittagong.
2 November 1667: the Ahoms recapture Guwahati.
1678-79: Aurangzeb ends the Marwar state.
1679: Marwar becomes crown territory.
March 1679: Guwahati is handed to the Mughals.
1680: the Mughal-Maratha Wars; Aurangzeb 'led campaigns from 1682 in the Deccan'.
1681: Durgadas begins to recapture Marwar.
1682: the Mughals are driven out at Itakhuli.
April 1685: the 1636 tribute relation ends when Aurangzeb declares war.
15 April 1685: the siege of Bijapur begins.
September 1686: Bijapur is annexed.
12 September 1686: the siege ends with the annexation.
1687: Golconda falls.
1687: Golconda is annexed, completing the conquest of the Deccan sultanates.
January 1698: Jinji (Gingee), the Maratha southern capital, falls to the Mughals ('until its fall in January 1698').
April 1700: 'Prayagji Prabhu's defence surrendered in April 1700, just before the onset of the monsoon' (the Satara defence); the page does not date Aurangzeb's conquest of Satara otherwise.
1707: Ajit Singh takes Jodhpur.
1707: Jodhpur is Ajit Singh's again (same sentence).
3 March 1707: Aurangzeb dies at Bhingar, ending the wars de facto.
February 1708: Bahadur Shah retakes Marwar.
1710: the Carnatic becomes independent of the Mughals.
1710: Bahadur Shah recognises Ajit Singh.
1717: Bengal becomes independent in fact.

c. 1720: Rohilkhand. The page's table gives c. 1720 for Rohilkhand under Ali Mohammed Khan; the state 'was formed by Afghan (Rohilla) military entrepreneurs'. Cliopatria keeps Rohilkhand in the Mughal shape to 1743.
1722: Awadh. Saadat Khan was 'appointed subahdar in 1722' and the page's table gives 1722 for Awadh's effective independence; Cliopatria's Awadh row begins 1727.
1724: the Nizam leaves the court.
7 January 1738: the Treaty of Bhopal cedes Malwa.
June 1738: Nader Shah invades.
June 1738: Ghazni and Kabul fall to Nader Shah; Cliopatria's Mughal shape drops them from 1738.
20 March 1739: Nader Shah enters Delhi.
16 May 1739: 'Nader and his Afsharid troops left Delhi on 16 May 1739.'
May 1739: the invasion ends with Karnal (24 February 1739), the sack of Delhi and the settlement of the Indus frontier.
May 1739: 'Nader Shah annexes all lands west of the Indus river'; before leaving he 'ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus, which he had overrun, to Muhammad Shah'.
1744: Cliopatria's Mughal shape drops 1.67 M to 0.54 M km2 between 1741 and 1744.
1752: Kashmir passes to Ahmad Shah Durrani.
3 April 1752: the Mughal-Afghan Wars end with the Punjab, Multan and Sindh under Ahmad Shah Durrani.
By 1760 the empire is 'Reduced subsequently to the region in and around Old Delhi' (after the Afghan sack of Delhi in 1757 and the Maratha capture of August 1757); Cliopatria's shape shrinks in 1762.
ledger.cp: Maratha, Jat and Rohilla successor states (page unnamed)

ledger.x: 1761: the Jats take Agra.
January 1772: Shah Alam II returns to Delhi.
1774: the Jat hold on Agra ends ('from 1761 till 1774'); the page does not name the new holder, and Cliopatria's 1783 shape has Agra again.
1783: 'The Mughal Empire disintegrated to such an extent that Shah Alam II was only left with Delhi city to rule.'
ledger.cp: Rajput, Maratha and Jat states (page unnamed)

ledger.x: July-August 1788: Ghulam Qadir holds Delhi.
16 October 1788: Shah Alam II's second reign begins.
May 1857: the sepoys reach Delhi.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 20-21 September 1857: the Siege of Delhi ends.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 21 September 1857: Delhi falls to the East India Company.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 7 October 1858: the last emperor is exiled to Rangoon and the dynasty ends.

wars.name: Mughal-Afghan Wars
wars.outcome: From Panipat (21 April 1526) to 3 April 1752: the Lodi fall, the Sur Interregnum of 1540-1555 and Humayun's return, and the Durrani take of the Punjab; the infobox closes the wars on 3 April 1752.

wars.name: Battle of Khanwa
wars.outcome: Mughal victory: Babur's forces defeated Rana Sanga's Rajput armies near Agra, 'a year later' than Panipat.

wars.name: Humayun's Gujarat campaign
wars.outcome: Humayun took Mandu and Champaner within a month in 1535; 'Bahadur Shah recaptured all of Gujarat in 1536 and began an attack on Malwa'.

wars.name: Sher Shah's war on Humayun (Chausa and Kannauj)
wars.outcome: Sher Shah won at Chausa (June 1539) and at Kannauj (17 May 1540); Humayun fled into fifteen years of exile and the Mughal Interregnum began.

wars.name: Humayun's reconquest of Hindustan
wars.outcome: Sikandar Shah Suri was defeated at Sirhind on 22 June 1555 and Humayun sat on the throne at Delhi on 23 July 1555.

wars.name: Second Battle of Panipat
wars.outcome: Bairam Khan defeated Hemu and the Sur army on 5 November 1556, securing Delhi-Agra for Akbar.

wars.name: Conquest of Malwa
wars.outcome: Baz Bahadur was beaten at Sarangpur in 1560; the Mughals annexed Malwa the following year.

wars.name: Mughal invasion of Marwar
wars.outcome: A twenty-year invasion (infobox span); Marwar returned as a Mughal-allied state; the page gives no dated sieges.

wars.name: Conquest of Garha
wars.outcome: Rani Durgavati was defeated at the Battle of Damoh and 'committed suicide'; Garha fell to the Mughals.

wars.name: Siege of Chittorgarh (1567-1568)
wars.outcome: 'Chittorgarh fell in February 1568 after a siege of four months'; Ranthambore followed in 1568.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Gujarat
wars.outcome: Akbar occupied Ahmedabad in 1572 and won a decisive victory on 2 September 1573.

wars.name: Battle of Haldighati
wars.outcome: Mewar 'was later defeated by the Mughals at the Battle of Haldighati in 1576'; no territorial result is on the page.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Bengal
wars.outcome: Patna was seized from Daud Khan in 1574, the Mughals won at Tukaroi in 1575 and Rajmahal (1576) ended the war; Orissa stayed a Karrani fief.

wars.name: Akbar's conquest of Kabul
wars.outcome: 'In August 1581, Akbar seized Kabul'; it became a province in 1585.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Kashmir
wars.outcome: An army was sent in 1585; Yaqub surrendered to Akbar at Srinagar in June 1589.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: 'Jani Beg surrendered to the Mughals in 1591'.

wars.name: Akbar's Deccan campaigns
wars.outcome: Operations began in 1593; Berar was ceded in 1595, Ahmadnagar fort taken in August 1600 and Asirgarh on 17 January 1601; Prince Daniyal governed the new subahs.

wars.name: Mughal-Safavid War (1622-1623)
wars.outcome: The Safavids took Kandahar on 22 June after a 45-day siege; the Mughals recovered it only in 1638.

wars.name: Shah Jahan's Deccan campaigns
wars.outcome: Daulatabad was captured in 1632 (1633 in a linked title) and the Nizam Shahi king imprisoned; 'Golconda submitted in 1635 and then Bijapur in 1636'.

wars.name: Fall of Kandahar (1638)
wars.outcome: Ali Mardan Khan handed Kandahar over to Shah Jahan; it stayed Mughal until 1649.

wars.name: Shah Jahan's Balkh and Badakhshan campaign
wars.outcome: 'They retreated from the fruitless lands, and Balkh and Badakhshan returned to Bukharan control'; Balkh was relinquished in 1647.

wars.name: Mughal-Safavid war (1649-1653)
wars.outcome: Safavid victory: Kandahar taken on 22 February 1649, Mughal sieges of 1649, 1651, 1652 and 1653 all failed (given up 29 September 1653).

wars.name: Mughal-Maratha Wars
wars.outcome: Bijapur and Golconda were captured by September 1686 (1687 for Golconda on the Aurangzeb page), Sambhaji on 1 February 1689, Jinji in January 1698; by 1705 the Marathas had crossed the Narmada and the Mughals were retreating in 1706.

wars.name: Nader Shah's invasion of India
wars.outcome: Nader Shah took Ghazni and Kabul (June 1738), won at Karnal on 24 February 1739, sacked Delhi from 20 March, annexed all lands west of the Indus and left on 16 May 1739 after handing back the lands east of the river.

wars.name: Durrani invasions of India (Punjab and Delhi)
wars.outcome: Sindh and the Punjab ceded to Ahmad Shah Durrani (1749 on the Durrani page, 1752 on the main and successor pages); Delhi sacked in early 1757 with Alamgir II left in nominal control.

wars.name: Battle of Buxar
wars.outcome: British victory on 22 October 1764; the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) gave the Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and the districts of Kora and Allahabad.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: 'On 14 September 1803 British troops entered Delhi ending the Maratha rule on the Mughals'; Shah Alam II came under British protection.

wars.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
wars.outcome: The sepoys proclaimed Bahadur Shah II at Delhi; the Siege of Delhi ended on 21 September 1857, Zafar was captured on 20 September, tried in 1858 and exiled to Rangoon on 7 October 1858.

wars.name: Ahom-Mughal conflicts
wars.outcome: The Mughals take western Assam by the Treaty of Asurar Ali (February 1639), lose Guwahati in 1658, retake it with Mir Jumla's invasion of 1662 (Ghilajharighat, January 1663), lose it on 2 November 1667, are handed it again in March 1679 and are driven back to…

wars.name: Siege of Bijapur (1685-1686)
wars.outcome: Aurangzeb declares war on Sikandar Adil Shah, who 'refused to become a vassal of the Mughal Empire'; the siege (15 April 1685 - 12 September 1686) ends with the annexation of the sultanate.

wars.name: Rathore rebellion in Marwar
wars.outcome: Aurangzeb makes Marwar crown territory in 1678-79; Durgadas recaptures 'vast expanses' from 1681 to 1687; Ajit Singh takes Jodhpur after Aurangzeb's death in 1707, Bahadur Shah retakes Marwar in February 1708, and in 1710 'recognized them as the rulers of…

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages opened for the Mughal frontiers (the Hindu Kush, the Rajput marches, the Deccan sultanates, Assam, Arakan); Cliopatria draws them approximately.

The Indus as the Mughal-Persian frontier from May 1739 ('all lands west of the Indus river') is a river line and the one firm frontier of the period, but the rest of the shrinking domain is approximate; Delhi city alone from 1783.
The emperor holds Delhi 'as far as Palam' under British protection; the limit is a place name, not a surveyed line.
